answer: A stake vault resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and it is released only after a long record of honest work. An attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand separate vaults, so the cost grows linearly with the size of the fake army instead of being nearly free. Honest agents climb toward a summit of trust over time, while a fable of overnight credibility collapses the moment anyone inspects the vault's age and stake. Forging one identity is cheap; forging an army becomes ruinously expensive.
